Model layer owns every §S-012 judgment: noteOverviewActive (transient, never persisted), entry releases zoom BEFORE showing and never changes focusedGroup, display set noteOverviewGroupIDs == WorkspaceState.visibleGroupIDs (canonical leaves = visible groups; hidden excluded), viewing-only guards (beginNoteEditing*, gotoGroupTarget, gotoGroupIndexTarget, switchFocusedGroup all no-op while active), toggle no-op while the note editor is open, restoreState/removeAllGroups end the mode. UI: per-group read-only GroupNoteOverviewOverlay inside each visible GroupView (lineLimit(maxNoteLines)+tail truncation in a group-bounded frame so layout never breaks; full text remains the edit overlay's job) plus workspace-level GroupNoteOverviewKeyCatcher (blocks the mouse; Esc via focused-field onExitCommand; re-pressed Cmd+Opt+N re-matched by a hidden keyboardShortcut button because SurfaceView.performKeyEquivalent ignores events while unfocused); exit hands first responder back to the terminal. 14 new model tests in GroupNoteTests.

decisions: restoreState (undo/redo) ends the overview rather than preserving it, so a restored snapshot's zoom can never contradict the mode's zoom-released invariant.
toggleNoteOverview is a no-op while the note editor is open: the editor owns the keyboard and its draft must not be silently dropped.

The overview's exit chord (Cmd+Opt+N) is re-matched by a hidden SwiftUI keyboardShortcut button hardcoded to the default binding; a user-rebound toggle_note_overview key would exit only via Esc — acceptable for the single-author product, worth a look at T-006.
